newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount to post $51 mln Q3 capital gain.
newsitem.headline: Discount to post $51 mln Q3 capital gain.

text.p: Israel's Discount Investment Corp said on Sunday it would record a capital gain of $51 million in the third quarter of 1997 from the sale of its stakes in Iscar Ltd and Blades Technology Ltd.

The shares were sold for $244 million to the Wertheimer family, which now owns 100 percent of Iscar and 50 percent of Blades. The remaining half of Blades is owned by jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, a subsidiary of United Technologies Corp.

Discount said that on Friday it sold 26.7 percent of Iscar for $197 million -- $131 million in cash and the rest in shares held by Iscar in IDB Holding Corp, Discount's parent company. The 2.94 million shares represent 7.8 percent of IDB.
As a result Discount will record an after-tax capital gain of $45 million.

Discount also sold 25 percent of Blades for 1.93 million shares in IDB, representing 5.1 percent of IDB's equity. The shares are worth $47 million and Discount will record an after-tax capital gain of $6 million.
Discount plans to sell the shares in IDB to institutional and other long-term investors.

Discount Investment managing director Dov Tadmor said in a statement that the proceeds from the sale would allow the company to continue with its investment strategy in areas such as telecommunications, high-technology and infrastructure.
